title: Budget Check
prompt:
**Scenario.** A problem has n ≤ 300000 and a 1 s limit (~3·10^8 ops ceiling). You have a correct O(n log^2 n) idea (≈ 3.3·10^8, borderline) and no O(n log n) idea yet. Best move?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Keep hunting for O(n log n) before writing anything

**B)** Code the O(n log^2 n) now; optimize later only if needed

**C)** Code O(n^2); it is simpler and surely correct

**D)** Give up the problem and move on

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: At ~3·10^8 the idea is code-it-now: the expected loss from more thinking usually exceeds the TLE risk. Code, test, and revisit only with time left.
